beseech.required_nuance: urgent pleading, from a position of weakness
beseech.mental_hook: Begging, in its most formal clothes.
beseech.semantic_hint: What a prisoner does to a judge for mercy.

incorrect_associations.misconception: hears 'seize' and swaps surrounding for taking

besiege.required_nuance: surrounding so as to force submission
besiege.mental_hook: Armies do it to cities. Letters do it to ministers.
besiege.semantic_hint: What an army does to a walled city it cannot enter.

incorrect_associations.misconception: keeps the literal dirt where reputation is meant

besmirch.required_nuance: staining a reputation, never a surface
besmirch.mental_hook: The dirt goes on a name, not a coat.
besmirch.semantic_hint: What a rumour does to a good name.

accepted_concepts: love-struck to the point of silliness

incorrect_associations.misconception: keeps the older sense and misses the infatuation

besotted.required_nuance: infatuation that has made someone foolish
besotted.mental_hook: In love, and not thinking straight.
besotted.semantic_hint: The word for someone so in love they have stopped making sense.

bestow.required_nuance: giving from a position of authority
bestow.mental_hook: Granted from above, usually with ceremony.
bestow.semantic_hint: What a monarch does with a title.

betoken.required_nuance: serving as a sign, often of what is to come
betoken.mental_hook: The thing that tells you what is coming.
betoken.semantic_hint: What dark clouds do with respect to a storm.

betray.mental_hook: You can betray a friend, and your face can betray you.
betray.semantic_hint: What a trembling hand does to the calm someone is pretending.

accepted_concepts: the person one is engaged to

incorrect_associations.misconception: confuses the engagement with the marriage
hears 'troth' as truth and misses the promise

betrothed.required_nuance: promised in marriage, not yet married
betrothed.semantic_hint: The old word for the person someone is engaged to marry.

accepted_concepts: a cluster of people or things

incorrect_associations.misconception: inverts a group into an individual

bevy.required_nuance: a group, usually all of one kind
bevy.mental_hook: A bevy of swans, or of consultants.
bevy.semantic_hint: The collective word for a whole group of swans arriving at once.

biased.required_nuance: leaning unfairly, not merely holding a view
biased.mental_hook: Not having an opinion. Tilting the scales.
biased.semantic_hint: What a report is when it quietly tilts toward one side.

accepted_concepts: separate into a pair of paths
bifurcate.semantic_hint: What a road does when it forks into exactly two.

bilious.mental_hook: The old medicine blamed the liver. The word stuck.
bilious.semantic_hint: The word for a temper so sour it was once blamed on the liver.

accepted_concepts: con someone out of what they are owed
bilk.required_nuance: cheating specifically out of money owed
bilk.mental_hook: Taking what was owed to someone else.
bilk.semantic_hint: What a conman does to investors who never see their money again.

blanch.required_nuance: going white, whether a face or a vegetable
blanch.mental_hook: Faces do it in fear. Almonds do it in water.
blanch.semantic_hint: What a face does at very bad news, and what a cook does to almonds.

bland.required_nuance: lacking character, in taste or in style
bland.semantic_hint: The word for hospital food, and for a speech that says nothing.

incorrect_associations.misconception: hears a vaguely similar word and guesses

blatant.semantic_hint: The word for a lie told so openly that nobody even pretends otherwise.

bleak.required_nuance: hopelessness in a scene or a prospect
bleak.mental_hook: A grey moor, or a grey forecast.
bleak.semantic_hint: The word for a moor in winter, and for a forecast with no good news in it.

accepted_concepts: a disease that ruins a crop
blight.required_nuance: the thing that ruins, whether disease or influence
blight.mental_hook: It killed the potatoes, and now it kills city streets.
blight.semantic_hint: What ruined the Irish potato crop, and what ruins a neighbourhood.

blighted.required_nuance: ruined by something that attacked it
blighted.mental_hook: Crops, streets and hopes all suffer the same way.
blighted.semantic_hint: How hopes are described when something has ruined them entirely.

accepted_concepts: unable to see the wider picture
blinkered.required_nuance: narrowness of view, taken from a horse's harness
blinkered.mental_hook: Named for what is strapped beside a horse's eyes.
blinkered.semantic_hint: What a horse wears to stop it seeing sideways, turned into an outlook.
